sources.citation: Blench, Roger M. & Martin Walsh. 2010 [draft dated Cambridge, 11 January 2010; file 'Vazimba vocabulary August 09']. The vocabularies of Vazimba and Beosi: do they represent the languages of the pre-Austronesian populations of Madagascar? Draft circulated for comment. 12 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. The paper re-tabulates every Vazimba lexical item in Birkeli 1936 (Table 1, c. 30 words, mostly fish/food/fishing terms) and the Beosi items (Table 2); no phonology, no accent/stress remark; only notes that 'Birkeli is very inconsistent with his vowel transcriptions'. Conclusion (p. 9): 'the Vazimba data is so exiguous and so scattered, that it is unlikely to constitute a significant record of a substrate vocabulary'. A few Beosi forms carry accent marks copied from Birkeli (bakàkà, falà, fisapé, mané) but nothing is said about them.

sources.note: The only primary source of Vazimba (and Beosi) words; Glottolog's most extensive 'description' (a wordlist or less). Some Beosi forms carry accent marks (bakàkà, falà, fisapé, mané) that might encode stress, but Blench & Walsh, who read it in full, report no phonological statement. Needed only to verify that nothing on accent exists.
